goodsIndustries.name: Agriculture, Forestry, Fishing & Hunting
goodsIndustries.analysis:
Agriculture, forestry, fishing and hunting sector GDP printed -1.4% month-over-month and +5.4% year-over-year in the January 2026 StatCan GDP-by-industry release, the strongest year-over-year reading among the 20 NAICS industry buckets.1 The U.S. Commerce Department's preliminary seventh administrative review set Canadian softwood lumber duties at approximately 25%, down from the prior 35%, with the final rate expected in August.2 Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada's Principal Field Crops Outlook projects 2026 canola acreage at 21.8M acres (+1.0%) and total wheat area at 26.7M acres (-1.1%); Manitoba canola area is projected +4.7% to 3.2M acres.3 China is expected to lower its canola seed tariff to approximately 15% from March 1, 2026.4

The Nutrien share-price proxy used for Saskatchewan and Alberta potash economics closed at $104.62, down 1.0% week-over-week but up 50.6% year-over-year.5 The project database tracks 17 agriculture and forestry projects totalling $5.47B declared, with the largest entries including a Quebec biofuel facility ($1.2B, Under Construction), the Saint John pulp mill upgrades in New Brunswick ($1.1B, Under Review), and the Hinton Pulp Mill Expansion in Alberta ($584M, Proposed).6 The BC Forests Minister statement on the softwood duty review is linked in policy.json to 21 projects spanning forestry, manufacturing, agriculture and oil and gas, with 12 forestry projects carrying $4.73B in parsed value.7 If the final August softwood duty lands near the preliminary 25% and the Chinese canola tariff proceeds at 15%, the 21 linked projects and $4.73B in tracked forestry capital would carry updated input-cost and market-access assumptions.

goodsIndustries.name: Mining, Quarrying & Oil/Gas Extraction
goodsIndustries.analysis:
Mining, quarrying and oil and gas extraction sector GDP printed +1.2% month-over-month and -0.1% year-over-year in the January 2026 StatCan GDP-by-industry release.1 WTI crude closed at $102.77/bbl for the March 31, 2026 reference date, while Cameco Corp, the listed uranium equity proxy, closed at $147.75, down 0.6% week-over-week and up 149.9% year-over-year.2,3 The Sprott Physical Uranium Trust closed at $27.55, up 3.5% week-over-week and 34.1% year-over-year.3

At PDAC 2026, the federal Minister of Energy and Natural Resources announced $3.6B in new programs, with up to $165.2M for 22 projects across eight provinces unlocking $434M in capital, plus a First and Last Mile Fund backed by $1.5B.4 Canada secured 30 new critical minerals partnerships unlocking $12.1B in mining project capital.4 Industry forecasts call for 5,709 wells drilled in 2026 (+3% year-over-year), with Canadian Natural Resources planning 448 new wells under a +3% production plan.5 The project database tracks 421 mining and oil and gas projects totalling $268.74B declared, and mining and O&G employment stood at 343,600 in January 2026.6 If the $3.6B federal program and $1.5B First and Last Mile Fund proceed on the announced schedule, the 22 PDAC-identified projects and the 30-partnership pipeline would carry specific dollar commitments tied to the 421 tracked sector projects.

goodsIndustries.name: Utilities
goodsIndustries.analysis:
Utilities sector GDP printed +0.6% month-over-month and -1.7% year-over-year in the January 2026 StatCan GDP-by-industry release.1 Ontario Power Generation reconnected Darlington Unit 4 to the grid in March 2026, completing a C$12.8B refurbishment C$150M under budget and four months ahead of schedule.2 Ontario is advancing the first of four Small Modular Reactors at Darlington, announced as a global first in commercial SMR deployment; OPG and Port Hope signed a Wesleyville agreement envisaging up to 10 GWe in February 2026.2 Alberta's expert panel to the Minister of Affordability and Utilities was due to deliver its final report on integrating nuclear by March 31, 2026.2

The TSX Infrastructure basket traded at $55.20, up 0.4% week-over-week and 29.8% year-over-year, while the URA uranium spot ETF printed $46.86, down 2.8% week-over-week but up 114.2% year-over-year.3 Utilities employment stood at 176,300 in February 2026.4 The project database tracks 824 utilities and power-energy projects totalling $522.89B declared, the largest bucket in the database by aggregate capital value.5 If the four-SMR Darlington program and the Wesleyville 10 GWe concept advance on the announced timelines, the 824 tracked utilities projects would reflect sequential status advances through 2026 and 2027, and the uranium price complex (+114.2% year-over-year on URA) would flow through SMR fuel supply economics.

goodsIndustries.name: Construction
goodsIndustries.analysis:
Construction sector GDP printed +1.1% month-over-month and +2.8% year-over-year in the January 2026 StatCan GDP-by-industry release, the only goods sector with a positive year-over-year reading outside agriculture.1 Prime Minister Carney launched the Build Communities Strong Fund on April 7, 2026, committing $51B federal over eight years (approximately $12B/year), with the Embleton Community Centre and Park in Brampton named as the first project; provincial matching is projected at approximately $17B, and the federal GDP lift estimate is $95B over the decade.2 CMHC reported February 2026 housing starts at 15,886 units (vs 14,420 in February 2025), with the seasonally adjusted annual rate reaching 250,900, up 4.5% from 240,148 in January; 2025 total starts were 259,028, up 5.6% versus 2024.3

Residential building permits totalled $7,968M and non-residential permits $5,378M in January 2026, and construction employment stood at 1,986,800.4 The SLX steel ETF proxy closed at $90.13, up 1.2% week-over-week and 48.9% year-over-year, a direct input cost for infrastructure and building construction.5 The project database tracks 2,196 construction-category projects totalling $258.36B declared; the 211 residential and real-estate projects tracked at $44.42B align with the 250,900 SAAR housing starts print.6 If the $51B Build Communities Strong Fund flows on the announced cadence and provinces commit the projected $17B match, the 2,196 tracked construction projects would carry updated funding attribution through the eight-year program window.

goodsIndustries.name: Manufacturing
goodsIndustries.analysis:
Manufacturing sector GDP printed -1.4% month-over-month and -4.6% year-over-year in the January 2026 StatCan GDP-by-industry release, the steepest year-over-year decline among goods industries.1 Manufacturing sales reached $68.7B in January 2026, a -3.0% month-over-month change per StatCan Table 16-10-0048; inventories reached $120.6B (+0.9% month-over-month), the inventory-to-sales ratio stood at 1.76, and unfilled orders were $114.8B (+0.2% month-over-month).2 StatCan cited transportation equipment and machinery as the largest drag on January manufacturing sales.2

Ford's Bécancour cathode plant is expected to begin production in 2026 with up to 45,000 tonnes CAM/yr, and the GM/POSCO Future M Ultium CAM plant is approximately two-thirds complete; the Northvolt and Umicore Kingston projects are on hold, and the Quebec government has committed $270M to the Northvolt project whose status is uncertain.3,4 The SLX steel ETF proxy closed at $90.13, up 1.2% week-over-week and 48.9% year-over-year, a direct input cost for primary metals and transportation equipment subsectors.5 The project database tracks 52 manufacturing-tagged projects totalling $67.39B declared, a thin bucket relative to sector weight; coverage of the battery and EV chemicals pipeline is partial.6 If Ford's Bécancour cathode plant commissions on schedule in 2026 and the GM/POSCO Ultium CAM plant reaches production in early 2026, the battery-chemicals subsector of the 52 tracked manufacturing projects would carry updated status attribution.
